transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-27
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jordan (CSM), Priya (SE) — Verdant: Linda, Mark, Sophie, Aisha

Summary (auto): Kickoff for Verdant Clinic onboarding to Redwood. Covered deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), SSO/KMS/compliance questions, initial success criteria and timeline. Agreed next steps: share docs, schedule security deep-dive, provision trial capacity.

Topics: onboarding plan; VPC & network setup; data residency & retention; pilot SLA & metrics; integration timeline

Transcript:
00:00 Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Samir from Redwood, joined by Jordan and Priya. Happy to kick off and run through plan.
00:12 Dr. Linda Harding: Hi Samir, thanks. We just want to make sure we cover security stuff early — SOC2, SSO, data retention, and also who owns keys.
00:22 Mark Ortiz: And we want to understand options. We have a tight latency requirement for triage workflows, and also cost sensitivity.
00:35 Jordan: Great, that aligns with typical onboarding. Quick high-level, Redwood offers hosted API for fast start, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict controls.
00:50 Sophie Nguyen: For initial pilot we probably want VPC peering, not full on-prem, we have AWS infra and can do peering if you support it.
00:59 Priya: Yep we do VPC peering and private control plane options. We'll need your network diagram and IP ranges. There are a few ways — peering or AWS PrivateLink depending on your security team.
01:12 Aisha Khan: Timeline-wise we want to be live for internal users in ~6 weeks, with a public pilot in 10. Is that feasible?
01:24 Samir: That's realistic for a pilot if we get network info and SSO details quickly. We'll support a phased approach: start with hosted to unblock devs, then switch traffic to Dedicated with autoscale for pilot as needed.
01:40 Mark: Can you explain tradeoffs? Latency vs cost especially. Our triage is latency-sensitive.
01:48 Priya: Sure. Hosted is easiest but multi-tenant; latency is normally low but less predictable under burst. Dedicated gives pinned GPU capacity, lower tail latencies and predictable token costs per hour. Private on-prem gives maximum control but longer setup time.
02:05 Dr. Linda: And data retention? We need to ensure PHI is never stored in logs and we have audit trails.
02:12 Jordan: We support configurable retention — by default transient token logs for debugging for X days but can disable logs, and we provide audit logs pulled to your SIEM. For PHI workloads we recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS.
02:28 Sophie: KMS integration — do you support AWS KMS/HSM? Our security requires keys under our control.
02:34 Priya: Yes we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS). For Private deployments we can support customer-managed HSM arrangements; for Dedicated we support customer KMS for encryption of storage and model cache keys.
02:50 Mark: Any certs? SOC2, ISO?
02:53 Samir: We are SOC 2 Type II and currently pursuing ISO 27001; we'll share compliance pack and SOC2 report after an NDA via the security portal.
03:08 Aisha: For SSO we use Okta. How does Redwood handle RBAC and SSO provisioning?
03:13 Jordan: Okta SAML and OIDC supported. We map groups to roles, can set RBAC at route or model level, and integrate with SCIM for user provisioning. We'll send the SSO quickstart doc.
03:25 Dr. Linda: We also want to see performance numbers on our payloads — typical messages are ~250 tokens, sometimes spikes to 1500.
03:33 Priya: Good to know. For 250 tokens, we can illustrate expected p95 latency on Dedicated — we'll run a short benchmark during the proof-of-concept. Can you share sample prompts and traffic estimates?
03:45 Mark: Right now pilots will do 50 qps sustained during peak but only for a subset of users.
03:52 Priya: That's useful; for 50 qps at 250 tokens we can recommend X GPUs in Dedicated — we'll quantify after we run the smoke test. I'll put together a batching/caching recommendation too.
04:05 Sophie: About integration — do you provide SDKs and webhooks?
04:08 Samir: Yes, REST and official SDKs; we also offer streaming responses and tool-calling if you need structured outputs. We can also hook events to your webhooks for usage and errors.
04:20 Aisha: Who is our main contact for technical onboarding?
04:22 Jordan: Priya will be SE lead, Samir is AE and Jordan will manage onboarding timeline and adoption.
04:30 Dr. Linda: That sounds good. A couple clarifying Qs — what happens if model regressions occur? We need guardrails.
04:38 Priya: We recommend setting up evals and regression monitoring tied to your prompt sets. Redwood Optimize can surface quality regressions and trigger alerts. For pilot we can run baseline evals and set thresholds.
04:50 Mark: Any rate limiting and quotas we should be aware of?
04:53 Samir: We'll set per-route quotas, and for the pilot we'll configure burst capacity. Also cost monitoring per token will be visible in the Console.
05:03 Sophie: For the VPC peering, what network config do you need?
05:06 Priya: We'll need VPC id, CIDR ranges, and a contact for firewall/IP allowlist. We'll send a template.
05:14 Aisha: On legal, we need a DPA and data processing terms. Who handles that?
05:18 Samir: Our legal team has a standard DPA; I can put you in touch. Procurement often wants timeline for the contract too — typically 2–3 weeks for standard terms.
05:30 Dr. Linda: For pilot success criteria: we want <200ms p95 for critical calls, error rate <0.1%, and cost under $X per thousand tokens — we'll define exact numbers.
05:42 Jordan: We'll help formalize those KPIs and instrument dashboards in Console. We'll also set up alerting.
05:50 Mark: Ok when do you need our network diagram and sample prompts?
05:53 Aisha: We'll aim to send the network diagram and sample prompt set by Monday 2026-08-31.
05:58 Priya: Perfect, that will let us schedule the VPC peering review and run initial smoke tests.
06:05 Samir: Recap of next steps: I'll send the onboarding deck, pricing and trial instructions; Priya will run the benchmark checklist; Jordan will schedule the security deep-dive; Aisha will provide network diagram — agreed?
06:18 Dr. Linda: Agreed. Also please include the SOC2 and SSO quickstart.
06:24 Samir: Will do. Any other questions?
06:28 Mark: One small thing — do you have any recommended quantization/ops guidance to lower costs for embeddings-heavy workloads?
06:34 Priya: For embeddings we suggest a mixed approach — run standard FP16 for quality-critical models and quantized for batch offline tasks. We'll share Optimize playbook.
06:45 Sophie: Ok, thanks everyone. Looking forward to the security call.
06:48 Samir: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.
06:52 [meeting ends]

Notes: Transcript has occasional transcription errors (names and acronyms may be slightly off). References to pricing use placeholders and will be replaced in formal docs.
